title: Buying Gold and Silver
body:
O.P.
Hey team,
I'm looking to make investments into Gold and Silver and I have a few questions for those gold and silver bugs out there...
Firstly, A recommendation as to a platform or way to buy G & S that is physically backed with a strong history of audits, reputable company/website etc. I'm probably not interesting in holding the physical gold myself as I am a bit of a clumsy fella. But really like the idea of my investment being backed 1:1 by the assets so that even if the company backing it fails, my investment is still safe.
Secondly, I'm a crypto fanatic and relatively young. So i'm used to seeing 5-10% moves daily and to be honest the lack of volatility in the traditional markets kinda bores me, but definitely appreciate the strong fundamentals behind G & S, especially with this current economic situation. So I was looking to also buy some using leverage also, recommendation as to platforms that allow leveraged trades that could be held for relatively long term periods.
It would be great if you could touch on why you feel your chosen platform is better than others also.
Many thanks!!!

---- replies ----
[User #10400215545 postscluster2Whirlpool Forums Addict] albinowhale writes...
Firstly, A recommendation as to a platform or way to buy G & S that is physically backed with a strong history of audits, reputable company/website etc.
https://www.perthmint.com/st orage/certificate-program.html
As for silver, its been in a bear market for many years now. I sold out when the price hit US$35 early this decade. It's currently sitting at under $17.
[User #7814585192 postsZeroDeltaWhirlpool Forums Addict] CME futures. You can trade them through Interactive Brokers, or any similar, reputable broker.
The contracts are physically deliverable, so they are bound to give you your gold/silver if you want it (and can pay for it).
Avoid any of the FOREX trading websites that offer metals, they are backed by nothing and could blow up without any notice.

[User #10400215545 postscluster2Whirlpool Forums Addict] albinowhale writes...
So you don't think silver could turn around? trading at near all time lows when you look at the silver:gold ratio
It's probably a better time to buy it now, when the price is low (relative to the last decade) with the hope it could go up. But silver and gold of course pay no dividends nor interest so you have to weigh that up as well.
For me it made sense to sell up all my gold and silver years ago and plough that money into my mortgage. Every year I was getting a guaranteed 4 to 6% return, after tax, by offsetting interest while gold and silver prices went down.
So, it could go up, down, or maybe stay level. I don't know :-)
[User #49106399 postsscroneParticipant] PMGOLD ETF traded on the ASX has a low carry cost but it's priced in AUD so you need to factor that in.
[User #1906116690 postsZed SurrealIt is.Whirlpool Forums Addict] albinowhale writes...
Firstly, A recommendation as to a platform or way to buy G & S that is physically backed with a strong history of audits, reputable company/website etc.
Google them, all Bullion dealers claim to be reputable, and there is no way that anyone here could verify that one way or the other. My advice is pick one, and go visit them.
Some notable ones in Australia are Ainslie Bullion. Gold Stackers, GBA (owns gold stackers), Perth Mint. The advantage of all of those apart from Perth Mint is more personalised service, its likely you will always deal with the same person. I recall that Ainslie bullion gave me better rates than what was published, and i didnt even ask. "because i was a good customer they said'
PMDS at Perth mint is not a bad deal for a large holding. there is no 1% fee on buy and sell if your holding is over $50k, so that actually makes it a good spot to hold pooled metals if you wanna do swaps. Though in saying that, i havent compared the rates with other dealers.

[User #49106399 postsscroneParticipant] Zed Surreal writes...
what do we need to factor in? we earn AUD and we hold AUD, so we need to buy with AUD.
Gold is partly a currency play, so if you're not considering the relative value of the Australian dollar when buying the PMGOLD ETF you've got rocks in your head. Alternatively you can by a USD hedged ETF like the Betashares Gold Bullion ETF (QAU).
